First listed 2025-07-07 · episode or wrap

Don't Get Fooled Again: Pulitzer Winner Warns of Wall Street's Dark Side

Eisman and journalist Gretchen Morgenson examine analyst conflicts, AIG accounting, mortgage securitization, dealer marks, due-diligence failures and private-equity incentives. Their strongest supported mechanisms concern compensation conflicts and the weakness of incomplete mortgage screening. Eisman rejects the claim that post-crisis banking never changed and explicitly refuses to forecast a private-equity or insurer collapse without data. Morgenson’s nursing-home and insurance warnings remain guest views. The audit qualifies retrospective accusations, sampling extrapolations and claims of absent regulation rather than treating indignation as proof.

YouTube automatic captions; speaker attribution requires context

Steve Eisman interviews Gretchen Morgenson. Direct agreement is recorded where explicit; her private-equity warnings are kept separate from his repeated refusal to predict a collapse.

  • Opening montage repeats later discussion.
  • The cash-in/cash-out swap anecdote contains explicitly uncertain contract recollections and invented numerical examples.
  • Clayton is sometimes captioned as Clayton Mortgage; the due-diligence firm is Clayton Holdings.
  • The guest corrects the suggestion that her reporting alone removed Greenberg.
  • Eisman corrects the guest’s nothing-changed claim and acknowledges available insurance statutory reports.
  • Neither participant gives a timed private-equity-collapse forecast attributed to Eisman.
